solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: B and D are weak distractors; B directly contradicts para 5 ('did not convert me to rhyme at any cost'). A is the only real pull: it restates the author's earlier view.
minor: R033-02's key ('a position the author later revised') hints at the change-of-view main idea in C.
R033-01.notes: Passage traces the author's shift from treating form as decoration to treating the shape as one of the statements, which led to a new translation practice in book two.

flags: minor: D's 'praised for accuracy' comes from para 3 (reviewed kindly / reader called them accurate), so it is a wrong-paragraph trap; acceptable.
R033-02.notes: Para 2 lays out the reasoning ('My reasoning seemed sound') for unrhymed translation, a view revised in paras 4-5. C describes para 6.

flags: minor: A contradicts the stated 'accurate'; C (music) is the only tempting distractor.
R033-03.notes: 'Told me what the poems say' = content; 'what they are like' = the experience/feel. She heard them sung.

flags: minor: 'opposing meanings' slightly overstates 'meant something close to its opposite'; still clearly best.
minor: answer is a fairly direct paraphrase of 'ear heard agreement while the mind heard argument ... lost the collision'; mostly a lookup.
R033-04.notes: B is a trap that reverses 'kept both words'. D is padding from para 2. C (meter) is never mentioned.

flags: minor: A and C are both literal-sense distractors that do the same job; D (repetition) is the only figurative competitor and is weak. Overlaps with R033-04, which tests the same 'collision' sentence.
R033-05.notes: Collision = clash of sound agreement against opposing meaning.

flags: minor: A, B and D are easily eliminated, and D contradicts para 6. C closely paraphrases the first two sentences of para 5.

Overlap: R033-06 and R033-09 both turn on 'Some of the strictly rhymed translations I had distrusted really are as bad as I thought'; R033-06's key ('still critical of many') signals the answer to R033-09 (D).
R033-06.notes: 'Did not convert me to rhyme at any cost'; 'really are as bad as I thought', yet he now uses rhyme selectively.

R033-07.notes: Near-rhymes and moved rhymes keep the echo/collision ('so that the collision still happened') without the forced end-rhyme padding. B is contradicted by the form purists saying he did not take enough liberties. C ('exactly') is wrong.

flags: minor: D ('thinks most criticism ... unfair') is the opposite of what is stated, and A is unsupported, so this is effectively a choice between B and C.
R033-08.notes: Both are right because the compromise loses some accuracy and some form: 'A translation is a set of losses chosen on purpose.'

flags: Overlap/giveaway: R033-06's key ('still critical of many') and its source sentence point to D here.

minor: B copies para 5's 'I now think of the shape as one of the statements' word for word as a distractor (it is an end-only belief), so students who match words will fall for it; A is a beginning-only belief. Good traps, but D requires noticing 'really are as bad as I thought' in para 5 and linking it to the padding in para 2.
R033-09.notes: Para 2 says forced rhyme fills with padding; para 5 says some strictly rhymed translations 'really are as bad as I thought.' A and C are beginning-only beliefs; B is end-only.
